subject: Business Models
title: Aggregator Theory
description: Learn Aggregator Theory in one minute.

hook.text: Google doesn't create content. Facebook doesn't create posts. They aggregate others' work and own the audience.

buildup.text: Ben Thompson's Aggregator Theory: internet companies win by owning the customer relationship, not the supply.

discovery.text: Aggregators attract users with free access, then use that audience power to dictate terms to suppliers.

twist.text: Newspapers create the content; Google captures the ad revenue. The aggregator's power exceeds the creator's.

climax.text: Aggregators become the most valuable companies because controlling demand is more powerful than controlling supply.

punchline.text: Own the audience, control the suppliers. Aggregators win the internet.

quiz.question: What does an aggregator control according to Aggregator Theory?

details.summary: Aggregator theory explains how internet platforms that own the customer relationship and aggregate supply gain disproportionate power. Aggregators like Google, Facebook, and Amazon attract users, which attracts suppliers, creating a virtuous cycle that concentrates market power.
details.whyItMatters: Aggregator theory explains why a few tech giants dominate their markets. Understanding this dynamic helps entrepreneurs recognize when aggregation effects apply and why competing with established aggregators is so difficult.
takeaways: Aggregators own the customer relationship and commoditize suppliers
Zero distribution costs on the internet enable winner-take-all dynamics
User acquisition drives supplier acquisition in a reinforcing cycle

faq.question: How is an aggregator different from a platform?
faq.answer: Platforms create value by facilitating direct interactions between users and third parties. Aggregators intermediate the relationship, controlling the user experience and commoditizing suppliers. Google aggregates content; an app store is a platform enabling direct distribution.

faq.question: Why are aggregators so hard to compete with?
faq.answer: They control demand through the user relationship. New suppliers must go through the aggregator to reach customers. Users stick because the aggregator has the most suppliers. This creates a reinforcing cycle that is nearly impossible to break from the outside.
